title.value: LF-PPL: A Low-Level First Order Probabilistic Programming Language for Non-Differentiable Models
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the development of a new probabilistic programming language called LF-PPL for non-differentiable models.
title.quote: LF-PPL: A Low-Level First Order Probabilistic Programming Language for Non-Differentiable Models

analysis.description: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic programming language, LF-PPL, which is designed for handling models with non-differentiable densities. The language supports efficient inference in such models by automatically detecting discontinuities and providing necessary information for implementing inference algorithms like Discontinuous Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (DHMC). LF-PPL aims to facilitate the integration of specialized inference algorithms in probabilistic programming contexts.

type.justification: The paper is primarily focused on the theoretical development of a new programming language and its underlying framework for handling non-differentiable models.
type.quote: Our story so far was developed by introducing a low-level first-order probabilistic programming language (LF-PPL) and its accompanying compilation scheme.

name.justification: The paper develops a low-level first-order probabilistic programming language designed specifically for probabilistic models with non-differentiable densities.
name.quote: In the context of probabilistic programming [3, 4, 5, 6] such densities are often induced via branching, i.e. if-else statements, where the predicates depend upon the latent variables of the model.

name.justification: The paper's proposed programming language LF-PPL incorporates Bayesian inference methods for handling models with discontinuities.
name.quote: LF-PPL enables one to incorporate a broader class of specialized inference techniques as automated inference engines. In doing so, it removes the burden from the user of manually establishing which variables the target is not differentiable with respect to.

name.justification: The paper implements Discontinuous Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (DHMC), a stochastic inference algorithm, as part of the framework.
name.quote: We realize this potential by implementing Discontinuous HMC (DHMC) [8] as an inference engine in LF-PPL, allowing for efficient, automated, HMC-based inference in models with a mixture of continuous and discontinuous variables.

name.justification: The paper discusses the implementation of DHMC as an inference engine within LF-PPL, showcasing its suitability for models with non-differentiable densities.
name.quote: We realize this potential by implementing Discontinuous HMC (DHMC) [8] as an inference engine in LF-PPL, allowing for efficient, automated, HMC-based inference in models with a mixture of continuous and discontinuous variables.

is_contributed.justification: The DHMC is not a new model contribution of this paper, but its implementation within LF-PPL is highlighted.
is_contributed.quote: Similarly, many variants of HMC have been proposed in recent years ... We realize this potential by implementing Discontinuous HMC (DHMC) [8] as an inference engine in LF-PPL.

is_executed.justification: The paper describes running DHMC as an inference engine within the LF-PPL framework.
is_executed.quote: We realize this potential by implementing Discontinuous HMC (DHMC) [8] as an inference engine in LF-PPL, allowing for efficient, automated, HMC-based inference in models with a mixture of continuous and discontinuous variables.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares the results of the implemented DHMC with PyMC3 NUTS with Metropolis-within-Gibbs for performance analysis.
is_compared.quote: We compared the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of the posterior estimates for the cluster means of both an unoptimized version of DHMC and an optimized implementation of NUTS with Metropolis-within-Gibbs (MwG) in PyMC3 [22].
